paper_style.palette_strategy: Figures 1–3 use a blue/orange instructional palette with gray/white structure; Figure 3 adds green/magenta for within-/outside-clip sampling. Figure 5 uses orange/gray/blue GSB segments. Figures 4 and 6–13 inherit photographic/illustrated scene colors, with white gutters and sparse dark labels. Native tables are grayscale with metric arrows and bold/underline highlights.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: All 13 Figures are raster JPEG/image XObjects; Figure 3 is the smallest at roughly 181 ppi in the PDF object, while the other imported composites range from about 268 to 1,849 ppi. Captions, table text, table rules, and surrounding prose are native PDF objects. No vector plot source was found.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman No9 L and Computer Modern math are stable for body, captions, and native tables; embedded figures introduce estimated sans-serif labels with variable sizes. Caption titles are consistently bold. Method diagrams share blue/orange role colors, tables share arrows and bold winners, and qualitative plates share white gutters, but appendix captions become title-only and Figure 10/11 captions are duplicated.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Simulating a Mind for Avatars. We model avatar behavior using dual-process theory, distinguishing between reactive (System 1) and deliberative (System 2) cognition. Top Right: Conventional methods, analogous to System 1, excel at reactive tasks like lip-sync but produce repetitive, non-contextual motions. Top Left & Bottom: In contrast, our framework simulates both systems, integrating System 2’s high-level reasoning to generate diverse, context-aware behaviors that are semantically aligned with the audio and text.

encodings.text: System 1/System 2 labels, task prompts, and panel headers

figures.evidence_relation: Introduction dual-process functional analogy → Figure 2 architecture and Figure 3 conditioning dilemma → Tables 1–4 objective/subjective comparisons → Figures 4–5 generalization and preference evidence.
design_strengths: Immediate baseline/proposed contrast makes the paper's headline story legible before the method details.
Panel position, headers, icons, arrows, and text redundantly encode the System 1/System 2 roles.
Examples span audio-only, text-plus-audio, non-human, and multi-person behavior.

No prompt/sample denominator or evidence-selection rule is attached to the qualitative claims.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a compact conceptual key with aligned baseline/proposed qualitative lanes, while adding an explicit sampling rule and a scope note for functional analogies.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: The Dual-System Simulation Framework. Our framework models avatar behavior by integrating a deliberative System 2 for planning with a reactive System 1 for synthesis. Left: Overall Pipeline. An MLLM-based System 2 reasons over multimodal inputs (audio, image, text) to generate a high-level “schedule”. This schedule guides the System 1 MMDiT, which synthesizes the final video by fusing information through dedicated text, audio and video branches. Right: Key Components. (a) The System 2 reasoning pipeline, comprising an MLLM Analyser and Planner. (b, c) Our proposed MM-Branch Warm-up and Pseudo Last Frame strategies, designed to mitigate modal conflicts.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: The Reference Conditioning Dilemma. Left: The evolution of reference conditioning methods towards simpler designs. Right: The core sampling trade-off. Sampling within-clip ensures high relevance but teaches the model to produce static results. figures.label: Figure 13

caption.text: Figure 13: Limitations of our method. Despite its strong performance, our method exhibits limitations in both synthesis and reasoning. On the synthesis level, the model can struggle with fine details during rapid movements, leading to hand artifacts (row 1) and degraded facial identity during large head turns (row 2). Separately, on the reasoning level, the agent can generate motions that, while plausible, are occasionally over-articulated (e.g., excessive gesturing), lacking the subtlety required for cinematic performance.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 frames the dual-system claim; Figure 2 makes the Analyzer/Planner–MMDiT interface concrete; Figure 3 motivates reference/PLF choices. Tables 1–4 establish component and benchmark comparisons, Figures 4–5 add generalization and preference cases, and Appendix Figures 6–12 extend reasoning, long-form, and semantic evidence. Figure 13 supplies the explicit failure boundary. The narrative is coherent but semantic claims rely heavily on selected qualitative exemplars.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use a bold title phrase followed by regular Nimbus Roman prose. Main Figures 1–6 and Tables 2–4 perform setup/comparison work; Appendix Figures 7–11 are title-only. Figure 6 says the corresponding reasoning process is provided although it appears on later pages, and Figures 10/11 reuse the same reflection caption while p.29 calls Figure 10 an MM-Warmup ablation.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Metric direction arrows are consistent. Tables 3/4 group subjective/quantitative or dataset blocks; Tables 1/2/5/6 use compact method/metric headers. Bold full-model/best cells communicate selection, but underline semantics and missing subjective values are not explained.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Table 1 isolates agentic reasoning and conditioning; Table 2 adds human semantic/artifact evidence; Tables 3–4 test multi-person and benchmark transfer. Appendix Figures 8–11 make PLF, MM-Warmup, and reflection visually inspectable, except that Figure 10's caption/callout mismatch breaks one mechanism link.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–4 point to Appendices C–E. Appendix C gives evaluation details, D gives reasoning/MLLM prompt and Tables 5–6, E gives qualitative ablations, F gives latency, and H gives failure cases. The appendix expands visual coverage but adds no uncertainty or denominator information.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Native PDF typography is consistent Nimbus Roman No9 L plus Computer Modern math. Raster labels vary in sans-serif sizing and become small in Figures 2, 5, 7, and 11; Figure 3 has visibly lower raster resolution.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue/orange encode System 1/System 2 and modules in Figures 1–3; quantitative tables use black/white, arrows, and bold/underline; qualitative figures inherit scene colors. Direct labels give partial redundancy, but there is no global legend and grayscale accessibility is weak for the instructional composites, Figure 5, and most image montages.

most_reusable_patterns: Dual-panel method diagrams that pair an end-to-end pipeline with enlarged component mechanisms.
Fixed-column qualitative grids aligning baseline/proposed outputs or long-form time points.
Two-level table headers that group subjective and objective evidence while retaining metric direction arrows.
Candid limitation plates that bound headline qualitative evidence.
failure_patterns: Qualitative selection without denominator, timestamp, prompt, or sampling rule.
No uncertainty or replicate information in any table or plotted preference object.
Title-only appendix captions and rasterized tiny labels.
Figure 10 MM-Warmup/reference mismatch and duplicated Figure 10/11 reflection captions.
Reliance on a few favorable examples for semantic-superiority claims.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses a blue/orange dual-system story, compact objective/subjective tables, and dense qualitative montages to argue that MLLM planning plus multimodal diffusion improves context-aware avatar motion, but every qualitative claim needs sampling/protocol metadata and uncertainty and the Figure 10/11 linkage needs repair.
